docs.title: Architecture and operation
docs.text:
All conversion entry points call streaming_writer.convert. XRMReader remains a pynxtools MultiFormatReader; format inspection and metadata mapping are separate from the pixel phase. ZeissSource reads the OLE directory and small header streams, then opens one image stream at a time. TiffSource adapts the existing TIFF manifest. No complete pixel volume is assembled. Header arrays and the OLE directory grow with frame count, so total metadata memory is not constant.

The standard pynxtools Writer creates metadata using the selected NXDL. Links to pixels are deferred until the HDF5 adapter has created their targets. Each frame is written to a fixed-size gzip dataset. Float reference images remain in separate NXdata groups with their original datatype. All non-image vendor streams and complete associated recipes are retained as base64 JSON in NXnote datasets. This preserves metadata stream bytes; it does not preserve the original OLE file layout or embed a byte-identical copy of the entire image file.

Output creation uses an exclusive per-output lock, a temporary file, NXDL and shape checks, and atomic replacement. Failed conversions preserve an existing valid output. Repeated conversion can reuse a validated result when source path/size/mtime, effective metadata, recipe, compression, application NXDL and implementation fingerprint match. The source pixel SHA-256 is recorded during writing; cache lookup uses file stamps rather than rereading gigabytes of pixels.

Input Dataset order Write operation TXRM / projection TIFF frame, column, row data[i] = frame.T TXM / reconstruction TIFF x, y-layer, z data[:, i, :] = frame.T XRM row, column data[:, :] = frame

TXM requires explicit image_orientation (row_axis=z, column_axis=x, signs +/-1). Its measured Y positions are checked against the single cubic voxel size. X/Z axes are local centered pixel offsets; the volume is related to the native sample frame through the stored stage transformations. TIFF volumes additionally require volume_origin_um, the first voxel coordinate in that frame. Raw TIFFs require a real theta array and one image_key per frame. No uniform angle series is generated. XRM pixel axes are local row/column distances with no asserted orientation in stage coordinates.

The global coordinate system uses X along the beam, source -X and detector +X, Y down, and right-handed Z. The sample basis is B @ Ry(theta), with B=[[0,0,1],[0,1,0],[-1,0,0]]. Native translations depend on the rotation chain. NXcoordinate_system explicitly relates this global frame to the NeXus default. Detector layout=area and type='planar area detector' record the user-confirmed geometry. Sensor pitch is never substituted for object-side pixel size.

docs.title: NOMAD deployment
docs.text:
Install the package into the app/worker environment to register xrm_raw_parser. Prepare an overlay with pynx-xrm definitions --output run/xrm-definitions. Set NEXUS_DEF_PATH to its absolute path before starting every app/worker process, and restart after plugin entry-point changes. The overlay is a copy of the installed definitions plus NXxrm_image; third-party package files are untouched. Its marker records the base revision and custom application checksum.

The binary MatchingParser checks extension, compound-file signature and ZEISS image headers without converting. The image mainfile owns conversion; an optional archive.yaml points at it with input_file and requests that owner to reprocess. Generated files use _nexus/<relative path>/<original name including extension>.nxs. Their processing is requested through NOMAD's process_updated_raw_file interface. Reused outputs do not trigger another generated-file processing request.

RCP matching uses explicit RecipePoint file declarations and acquisition directory context. The nearest unambiguous eLabFTW scope is used. Multiple matching metadata files or recipes require explicit assignment. Server inputs must remain inside the upload root; original absolute ZEISS paths are retained only as provenance. Adding/changing RCP or JSON later requires reprocessing the upload. There is no custom sidecar watcher or hidden background conversion service.

data:
  m_def: pynxtools_xrm.nomad.schema_packages.schema.XRMDataConverter
  tiff_directory: layers
  metadata_file: metadata.json
  target_definition: NXtomoproc
  output: result.nxs
  metadata_supplements:
    theta: 0
    stage_x_um: 0
    stage_y_um: 0
    stage_z_um: 0
    volume_origin_um: [-0.75, -0.5, -0.5]
    image_orientation: {row_axis: z, column_axis: x, row_sign: 1, column_sign: 1}

The geometry values above are a synthetic example, not defaults for measurements. Reconstruction program/version/date and source name/type must be supplied by genuine metadata.

docs.title: Metadata mapping and strict validation
docs.text:
Effective precedence is image > associated RCP > eLabFTW > explicit missing values. Conflicting lower-priority values remain in provenance. Explicit configuration cannot change an existing value. Invalid high-priority metadata are not replaced. RCP settings are preserved as recipe settings; nominal angle limits are never used to fabricate measured angle arrays. All RCP streams remain recoverable from entry/recipe/data (JSON with raw_streams_base64).

Required content NXtomo NXtomoproc NXxrm_image ZEISS source Sample name yes yes yes assigned RCP SampleName or ELN/config Image pixels / dimensions / datatype yes yes yes ImageInfo and ImageData blocks Theta and stage X/Y/Z profile profile profile Angles, X/Y/ZPosition; TXM MeanSampleX/Y/Z Rotation angle array / image_key yes no no measured Angles; primary TXRM projections key=0 Cubic object pixel/voxel size optional yes yes ImageInfo/PixelSize (um) Source name / type optional yes optional explicit proven source; numeric SourceType not decoded Reconstruction program/version/date no yes no missing in inspected TXM; no exeVersion/date fallback Raw acquisition file no yes no ReconSettings/InputFileName or assigned RCP Physical image orientation local axes yes local axes explicit calibrated row/column axes and signs Volume origin no TIFF required no explicit TIFF origin; measured TXM Y plus local X/Z offsets

The NXDL validator is authoritative for the pinned application contract. Profile requirements add geometry and provenance checks. Missing fields are reported together by MissingRequiredMetadata before output creation where possible.

Optional metadata Destination / handling XrayVoltage, XrayCurrent, ExpTimes NXsource voltage/current, detector count_time Acquisition ImageInfo/StoRADistance, DtoRADistance Signed X transformations in mm; never sample-center distance TXM ReconInputTomoParams/StoRADistance, DtoRADistance Positive magnitudes in um, converted to mm and placed on the confirmed global axis: source -X, detector +X. TXM ImageInfo distances are not decoded using the acquisition convention. CameraName, CameraSerialNumberString Detector description and serial_number ObjectiveName, SourceFilterName instrument/optics/objective and instrument/filter/description; manufacturer bytes retained ImageInfo/Date Berlin frame_times in provenance; first projection timestamp as start_time TXM ImageInfo/Date Layer timestamps retained; never asserted as reconstruction process time CamPixelSize Sensor pitch retained distinctly from object voxel/pixel calibration IsFlatPanel and unknown vendor fields Raw stream bytes with original OLE paths eLabFTW identity/project/sample/users/notes NXentry, NXsample, NXuser and NXnote Additional acquisition/reconstruction/storage fields Native scalar/array datasets in optional domain NXcollections; no serialized eLabFTW JSON

All full local timestamps use Europe/Berlin, with real UTC conversion for aware values. Full timestamp fields reject date-only strings, DST gaps and ambiguous local times. The optional acquisition/measurement_date preserves a calendar date without inventing a time. Original ZEISS bytes and the RCP recipe remain as provenance notes. Conversion time is the actual new conversion time and is distinct from acquisition/reconstruction time.

The eLabFTW field registry is maintained in elabftw.py. Standard NXsample, NXsource, NXdetector, NXfilter, NXuser, NXentry and NXprocess fields are used where their semantics match. Additional fields live in named domain NXcollections, which are optional base-class extensions rather than required application fields. Instrument item identifiers are resolved to names only through an exact linked record match. Multiselect text fields remain native UTF-8 arrays. Form settings, access control, history and UI fields have no verified domain destination and are listed individually in metadata_provenance/elabftw_mapping (source_path, target_path, status, reason). Empty fields are reported separately. Unknown populated extra fields retain their native value/unit under unmapped_metadata. The original eLabFTW JSON is not embedded, including in the provenance group. Lower-priority conflicting values and selected field origins are native datasets.

The single-image profile is a local application named NXxrm_image using generic NXimage and NXdata; it does not mislabel X-ray microscopy as electron microscopy through NXem. Its NXDL is packaged and added to an explicit definitions overlay.

docs.title: Windows: ZIP upload requires a second processing run
Summary
docs.text:
On a locally hosted NOMAD Oasis running on Windows, an uploaded ZIP archive can be extracted successfully but still leave the upload workflow in the failed state. Starting Reprocess a second time then succeeds.

This is not an error in XRMDataConverter or in the generated NXtomoproc file. The failure happens earlier, while NOMAD imports and removes the temporary ZIP archive. The observed exception is a Windows file-locking error:

PermissionError: [WinError 32]
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process:
.../.volumes/fs/tmp/<upload-id>/<upload>.zip

The problem was reproduced with both a small synthetic XRM upload and the complete AvCarb_FLEX_20bar.zip upload. It is relevant primarily to local Windows development. A production Oasis running on Linux is normally not blocked by this particular symptom because Linux permits unlinking an open file. The underlying file handle should nevertheless be closed explicitly.

docs.title: Observable processing sequence
docs.text:
The first workflow proceeds as follows:

  1. NOMAD receives the ZIP in its temporary upload directory.
  2. StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() recognizes and extracts the ZIP.
  3. All JSON, TIFF, and *.archive.yaml files are copied into the staging raw directory.
  4. NOMAD leaves the archive filesystem context.
  5. NOMAD attempts to delete the temporary ZIP.
  6. Windows rejects the deletion because the outer fsspec file handle is still open.
  7. The update_files_activity and therefore the first upload workflow fail.

The extracted files remain in staging despite that failure. During the second processing run NOMAD operates on these existing raw files, the archive parser loads the XRM entry, and XRMDataConverter.normalize() can produce and register the .nxs file successfully.

The important distinction is therefore:

First run:  ZIP import -> extraction -> temporary ZIP deletion fails
Second run: existing raw files -> archive parser -> XRM normalizer succeeds

docs.title: 1. NOMAD opens the archive with fsspec
docs.text:
The relevant context manager is FSUtility._open_archive_fs() in:

packages/nomad-FAIR/nomad/files.py

At NOMAD commit 2ddd7fb88711ab30b97b88a70c48e93be5b6ebd3, the local helper closes the archive filesystem after yielding it:

def _wrap(_fs):
    yield _fs
    if hasattr(_fs, "close"):
        _fs.close()

Reference: nomad/files.py in NOMAD

There are two issues with this implementation:

  • cleanup is not protected by try/finally, so an exception raised by the caller could bypass _fs.close();
  • ZipFileSystem.close() does not close the owning fsspec.core.OpenFile object that was opened when the ZIP filesystem was constructed from a path.

docs.title: 2. NOMAD extracts the ZIP
docs.text:
StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() opens the ZIP through FSUtility.open_archive() and copies all archive members:

if archive_format == "zip":
    with FSUtility.open_archive(path, fs=target_fs) as _fs:
        yield "", "", _fs

Local reference:

packages/nomad-FAIR/nomad/files.py:1766

docs.title: 3. NOMAD deletes the temporary source
docs.text:
After extraction, the same method removes the temporary upload file:

finally:
    if cleanup_source_file_and_dir:
        self._fs.rm(path, recursive=True)

Local reference:

packages/nomad-FAIR/nomad/files.py:1810

On Windows this removal raises PermissionError while the source ZIP still has an open handle.

docs.title: 4. fsspec keeps a separate owner object
docs.text:
When ZipFileSystem receives a path, its constructor creates an fsspec.core.OpenFile, enters that context, and stores both the owner and the opened file:

fo = fsspec.open(fo, mode=m, protocol=target_protocol, **target_options)
self.of = fo
self.fo = fo.__enter__()
self.zip = zipfile.ZipFile(self.fo, mode=mode, ...)

Its explicit close() method closes self.zip, while closing self.of is handled separately by the destructor. Garbage collection is not guaranteed to run before NOMAD tries to delete the temporary archive.

References:

  • fsspec ZipFileSystem
  • fsspec OpenFile

docs.title: Why XRMDataConverter is not the cause
docs.text:
The XRM normalizer is invoked only after NOMAD has imported the upload and the archive parser has parsed the *.archive.yaml mainfile. Its implementation is located in:

packages/pynxtools-xrm/src/pynxtools_xrm/nomad/schema_packages/schema.py

The converter starts at XRMDataConverter.normalize() and invokes convert_tomoproc() before registering the finished output through process_updated_raw_file():

report = convert_tomoproc(
    metadata,
    tiffs,
    output,
    compression=CompressionConfig(...),
    overwrite=True,
)

archive.m_context.process_updated_raw_file(self.output, allow_modify=True)

References:

  • XRMDataConverter.normalize()
  • convert_tomoproc()

The recorded failing Temporal activity was update_files_activity, and its traceback ended in StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() while deleting the temporary source ZIP. It did not end in XRMDataConverter.normalize().

docs.title: Reprocess the upload
docs.text: For local development, manually starting Reprocess again works because the first attempt already copied the archive members into staging. This is useful for testing but should not be treated as a production solution.

docs.title: Use TAR instead of ZIP on Windows
docs.text:
Uploading a .tar or .tar.gz archive avoids the affected ZIP filesystem branch. NOMAD reads TAR input inside an explicit file context:

with target_fs.open(location, "rb") as file:
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=file, mode="r|*") as tar:
        ...

The file context is closed before cleanup attempts to remove the temporary archive.

docs.title: Run the development Oasis on Linux or WSL
docs.text: The intended production environment is Linux. Running the development worker inside Linux or WSL also avoids the immediate Windows unlink restriction. Explicitly closing the resource remains preferable because it avoids leaking a file descriptor.

docs.title: Proposed NOMAD-Core fix
docs.text:
The durable fix belongs in NOMAD Core's FSUtility._open_archive_fs(), not in pynxtools-xrm. The wrapper should always execute cleanup and should also close the owning OpenFile for a ZipFileSystem:

def _wrap(_fs):
    owner = getattr(_fs, "of", None)
    try:
        yield _fs
    finally:
        if hasattr(_fs, "close"):
            _fs.close()

        # ZipFileSystem.close() closes the ZipFile but, when constructed from
        # a path, the owner returned by fsspec.open() must also be closed.
        if isinstance(_fs, ZipFileSystem) and owner is not None:
            close_owner = getattr(owner, "close", None)
            if callable(close_owner):
                close_owner()

Before submitting this upstream, the patch should also be checked for ZIP write and append modes and for non-local filesystems. The fix must not prematurely close a caller-owned file object.

An alternative implementation is to make the ownership explicit when creating the ZipFileSystem: open the source file in an outer with block, construct the ZIP filesystem from that file object, and close the ZIP filesystem before leaving the outer block.

docs.title: Suggested regression test
docs.text:
A regression test should verify both the resource state and actual Windows deletion behavior. The resource assertion also catches the problem on Linux, where unlinking an open file would otherwise hide it.

import zipfile

from nomad.files import FSUtility


def test_open_archive_releases_source_file(tmp_path):
    archive_path = tmp_path / "upload.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path, "w") as archive:
        archive.writestr("metadata.json", "{}")

    with FSUtility.open_archive(str(archive_path)) as archive_fs:
        assert archive_fs.cat("metadata.json") == b"{}"
        source_file = archive_fs.fo

    # This assertion detects the leaked owner on every operating system.
    assert source_file.closed

    # On Windows this operation raised WinError 32 before the fix.
    archive_path.unlink()
    assert not archive_path.exists()

A second integration test can exercise StagingUploadFiles.add_rawfiles() with cleanup_source_file_and_dir=True:

def test_add_rawfiles_removes_temporary_zip(staging_upload_files, tmp_path):
    archive_path = tmp_path / "upload.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path, "w") as archive:
        archive.writestr("metadata.json", "{}")

    staging_upload_files.add_rawfiles(
        str(archive_path),
        cleanup_source_file_and_dir=True,
        auto_decompress=True,
    )

    assert staging_upload_files.raw_path_exists("metadata.json")
    assert not archive_path.exists()

docs.title: Verification checklist
docs.text:
After applying a NOMAD-Core fix:

  1. Start the local Oasis on Windows.
  2. Upload a fresh ZIP containing an XRM *.archive.yaml, metadata JSON, and a small numbered TIFF stack.
  3. Confirm that update_files_activity completes successfully.
  4. Confirm that the temporary ZIP disappears from .volumes/fs/tmp.
  5. Confirm that the archive entry and generated .nxs entry both reach SUCCESS during the first workflow.
  6. Confirm that the .nxs volume retains its expected shape, dtype, chunks, and gzip compression.

docs.title: Scope decision for pynxtools-xrm
docs.text:
No workaround is currently added to XRMDataConverter, because:

  • the error occurs before the converter is invoked;
  • the target production Oasis runs on Linux;
  • changing the converter cannot release a file handle owned by NOMAD's upload layer;
  • the appropriate permanent correction is in NOMAD Core or fsspec resource handling.

This document records the issue so that it can be revisited if Windows becomes a supported deployment target or if the same resource leak appears in another environment.

docs.title: Note on versioning
docs.text: Keeping track of versions is essential for every software and semantic data modeling activity. We follow PEP440 when reporting versions, fetching metadata at run time using importlib.metadata. Several versions need to be distinguished. The version of pynxtools, the one of the NeXus definitions, and those of h5py and the HDF5 library. See the respective section of the pynxtools documentation that explains where these versions can be found.

docs.title: pynxtools-plugin version
docs.text: We consider it best practice that also each plugin of pynxtools writes its version as a programID instance of NXprogram. ID serves as a placeholder that can be either omitted or replaced by an integer if multiple programs need to be distinguished. Counting should start at one, i.e., program or program1 are preferred options. Specifically, the field program inside the programID instance should store the distribution (package) name. The attribute program/@version should store a version string following PEP440.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Structure of the pynxtools-xrm repository

The software tools are located inside src/pynxtools_xrm. They are shipped with unit tests located in tests.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
It is recommended to use python 3.12 with a dedicated virtual environment for this package. Learn how to manage python versions and virtual environments. We recommend using uv, an extremely fast Python package and project manager. In this tutorial, you will find parallel descriptions, using either uv or a more classical approach using venv and pip.

Start by creating a virtual environment:

uvvenv

uv is capable of creating a virtual environment and install the required Python version at the same time.

uv venv --python 3.12

Note that you will need to install the Python version manually beforehand.

python -m venv .venv

That command creates a new virtual environment in a directory called .venv.

docs.title: Development installation
docs.text:
We start by cloning the repository:

git clone https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/pynxtools-xrm.git \\
    --branch main \\
    --recursive pynxtools-xrm
cd pynxtools-xrm

Next, we install the package in editable mode (together with its dependencies):

uvpip 
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

Note that you will need to install the Python version manually beforehand.

pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Linting and formatting
docs.text:
We are using ruff and mypy for linting, formatting, and type checking. It is recommended to use the pre-commit hook available for ruff which formats the code and checks the linting before making a Git commit.

Install the precommit by running

pre-commit install

from the root of this repository.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
There exist unit tests for the software written in pytest which can be used as follows:

pytest -sv tests

docs.title: Editing the documentation
docs.text:
We are using `mkdocs for the documentation. If you edit the documentation, you can build it locally. For this, you need to install an additional set of dependencies:

uvpip 
uv pip install -e ".[docs]"

pip install -e ".[docs]"

You can then serve the documentation locally by running

mkdocs serve

docs.title: Contributing to the package on GitHub
docs.text: Once you are happy with the changes, please commit them on a separate branch and create a pull request on GitHub. We run a number of GitHub actions that check the correct linting, run the tests in an isolated environment, and build the documentation. Once these pass and a peer review of the code has occurred, your code will be accepted.

docs.title: Developing pynxtools-xrm as a NOMAD plugin
docs.text: If you plan to contribute to the NOMAD plugin functionality of pynxtools-xrm, it often makes sense to use the NOMAD development environment called nomad-distro-dev. You can learn more in the NOMAD documentation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If you face any issues with the tool or when setting up the development environment, please create a new Github Issue.

docs.title: How to install pynxtools-xrm with NOMAD
docs.text: Install it in the same environment as nomad-lab, prepare the definitions overlay, and set NEXUS_DEF_PATH to its absolute path before starting the app and workers. See architecture and deployment for the commands. Restart the processes after installing the new parser entry point. All processes must use the same definitions; the package does not modify installed third-party files.
